body: Wouldn't be better to fully expand it, instead of shrinking it?

You would think... but the maximum size prevents anything from actually happening. This would require making the maximum y value -1, which would cause the style to be different from what @jaydensipe intended. Here is how it would look with the maximum size removed and it set to expand next to a ShrinkCentered one I do quite like this a bit more, but this does have the side effect of making the Embedded Game toolbar incredibly chonky due to the use of labels inside the toolbar. before: after: This seemed to be an intentional thing, so I didn't want to change jayden's style.

Yeah, this is the issue I fought as well. The game toolbar is the outlier and we did not want to to be that thick, as it differs from the other toolbars. 

We could add another field to cap the maximum size if passed a flag, and only use that on the part of the toolbar with the labels?

That's what I was thinking, but the issue with maximize size is that it prevents the toolbar from growing if the user has an increase font-size, which would result in everything scaling correctly except the Input/2D/3D toolbar, which would be trapped We could try to introduce a scaling algorithm that reduces the font size of these labels based on the current editor size, however I'm not really sure what the math on that would look like, but with a label shrunk to fit the size of the toolbar's normal size, it would look quite thin (14 -> 11 font size) _We coulddddd_ sweep the problem under the rug and get rid of the labels and disallow labels in toolbars, and just have the mode switches be icons only :upside_down_face:
Actually. I think have a solution, let me try something...

So my solution involves creating a temporary label at the beginning of the toolbar, and then getting the maximum size of the toolbar afterwards. Since the height of the toolbar scales with the font-size, this would result in an accurate maximum height, and then we can apply this value to these new toolbars, thus giving a height that will scale with font-size correctly, but not cause the labels to shrink or expand the rest of the toolbar. 
The issue, as you're probably assuming, is that creating a label that I only use to get the size of the panel, and then immediately throw away seems a little wasteful, but I'm not really sure how you would otherwise go about it... It would additionally add a rather confusing extra step to plugin developers looking to use this new style as well, I'm really not sure here (Unless we do the test within the ToolBar's create method, but this would require guesswork on figuring out what the true toolbar parent is)

I think it's better to just go with the path of least resistance for now, shrinking it is.

However, I think the issue of toolbar groups not adjusting for larger fonts should be addressed. Would picking the bigger value between the default max size and the font size be enough to fix it?

Unfortunately no, since the font-size isn't really that closely related to the max size of the toolbar, a font size of 30 for instance results in the ideal height of the Game Toolbar to be 58, for reference, the default maximum size is 32. 
I can't think of any cheap tricks off the top of my head that would give us something that works, other than what I mentioned about a temp label.
Perhaps there is a misunderstanding, I'm referring to the font _inside_ toolbar groups, and if the maximum size of those can be overridden with the font height, if bigger.

Actually, if we do something like 
`MaximumSize.y = min(32, fontsize + margin + button.contentmargins)`
It would scale a _bit_ better, but since the size isn't exact this would result in the same issue where it would be off-center, since there's no way to vertically fill _and_ center, unless we also force this value to be our minimum size as well

> Perhaps there is a misunderstanding, I'm referring to the font _inside_ toolbar groups, and if the maximum size of those can be overridden with the font height, if bigger. I'm not entirely sure what you mean still I think? The font inside the groups is the same size as the rest of the editor (dependent on the setting), if you mean setting the button for these labels to be a min size of 32 that would work, but it would cause the button's size to be a little wonky, it does work though, I think the solution here may be to go forgo the Button node entirely and create a unique button? Ignore the rest of the elements not being scaled up I'm on a different branch, this results in the Game bar being the same size as the 2D and 3D toolbars, due to the buttons being constrained and prevented from expanding the toolbar, assuming that we remove the maximum size constraint from the toolbar itself, which will cause all the toolbars across 2d and 3d to become a little bit fatter
Lets not overcomplicate things, just taking into account the font height for max (and min) values will do for now.

So to be clear, the solution here should be to make the maximum height of the toolbar (or just the buttons?) match the font size? I'm a bit confused on what font size alone will do if not combined with other values, as it'll cause all the toolbars to shrink massively (32 -> 14)
I'm saying that, if possible, check between the default (32) and the font height combined with the other elements to see which is bigger, then use that value.
Is this necessary to be in the constructor too? The theme notification will always be called anyway.
Feels brittle to rely on two magic numbers at once, one was already not great. At the very least, there should be comment explaining what they mean.
CC @jaydensipe.
I found 32 * EDSCALE to match around the height of what the previous toolbars were.
Thanks!
Did not know that, it does indeed seem to be unnecessary, thanks!
